questions.topic: Artificial Satellites and ISRO
questions.question: Which statement about space debris is NOT correct?
options: Debris could collide with working satellites
Debris includes old satellites and their rocket parts
All debris burns up completely before reaching the ground
Countries are working together to remove the dangerous debris
questions.explanation: Small debris burns up in the atmosphere, but larger pieces can crash on the ground — so not all of it burns up. The other statements are given in the chapter.

questions.topic: Artificial Satellites and ISRO
questions.question: Who is known as the Father of the Indian Space Programme?
options: Meghnad Saha
Homi Bhabha
A. P. J. Abdul Kalam
Vikram Sarabhai
questions.explanation: Vikram Ambalal Sarabhai (1919–1971), a researcher in space science and nuclear physics, pioneered the effort to launch India's first artificial satellites and is called the Father of the Indian Space Programme.

questions.topic: Artificial Satellites and ISRO
questions.question: AstroSat is the ISRO satellite that captures images of the Earth's terrain for making maps.
questions.explanation: False. Earth imaging for maps is done by the Cartosat series; AstroSat makes scientific observations of stars and other celestial objects.

questions.topic: Artificial Satellites and ISRO
questions.question: Most artificial satellites take roughly 100 minutes to complete one orbit of the Earth.
questions.explanation: True. The chapter states most satellites orbit about 800 km up and take roughly 100 minutes per orbit.

questions.topic: Artificial Satellites and ISRO
questions.question: Select the TWO correctly paired ISRO missions.
options: Mangalyaan — mission to Mars
Chandrayaan — mission to Mars
Aditya L1 — studies the Sun
AstroSat — landing on the Moon
questions.explanation: Aditya L1 studies the Sun and Mangalyaan went to Mars. Chandrayaan 1, 2 and 3 were Moon missions, and AstroSat is an orbiting observatory, not a lander.

questions.topic: Artificial Satellites and ISRO
questions.question: Which statement about spotting satellites is NOT correct?
options: Satellites appear as tiny specks moving across the night sky
Satellites can be seen only through large telescopes
Mobile apps and websites can tell when a satellite will pass overhead
Satellites may show steady or flickering brightness as they move
questions.explanation: The chapter says satellites can be seen with the naked eye or binoculars — no telescope is needed. The other three statements come straight from Activity 11.4 and section 11.4.

questions.topic: Artificial Satellites and ISRO
questions.question: Both the Moon and an artificial satellite orbit the Earth. Using the chapter's numbers, how do their orbital periods compare?
options: The Moon takes about 100 minutes; a typical satellite about a month
Both take about 24 hours, matching the Earth's rotation
The Moon takes about a month; a satellite only about 100 minutes
The Moon takes about a year; a typical satellite about a day
questions.explanation: The Moon revolves around Earth in about a month (its phase cycle is ~29.5 days), whereas most artificial satellites at ~800 km complete an orbit in roughly 100 minutes.

questions.topic: Why Phases Happen: The Ball-and-Lamp Model
questions.question: We can only see that part of the Moon which reflects sunlight towards us.
questions.explanation: True. The Moon shines by reflected sunlight, and only the illuminated portion that faces Earth can be seen from here.

questions.topic: Moon's Orbit, Moonrise Delay, Eclipses and Tides
questions.question: The shadow of the Earth blocks sunlight from reaching the Moon, causing its phases.
questions.explanation: False. Earth's shadow on the Moon causes a lunar eclipse. Phases are caused by the changing fraction of the Moon's sunlit half that faces Earth as the Moon revolves.

questions.topic: Month, Year and Lunar Calendars
questions.question: Calendars are based on various astronomical cycles which repeat in a predictable manner.
questions.explanation: True. The day, month and year come from the predictable cycles of Earth's rotation, the Moon's phases and the seasons.

questions.topic: Locating the Moon in the Sky
questions.question: The Moon can only be seen at night.
questions.explanation: False. Meera saw the Moon in the daytime, and the chapter explains that a Moon rising in the afternoon can be seen in the eastern sky during daylight.

questions.topic: Phases of the Moon: Waxing and Waning
questions.question: Match the descriptions with the phases: (a) three days after new Moon, (b) a week after full Moon.
options: (a) a waning gibbous Moon; (b) a thin waxing crescent
(a) a full Moon; (b) a new Moon
(a) a waning half Moon; (b) a thin waxing crescent
(a) a thin waxing crescent; (b) a waning half Moon
questions.explanation: Three days after new Moon the bright part has just begun to grow — a thin waxing crescent. A week after full Moon the bright part has shrunk to a half circle — a waning half Moon.

questions.topic: Phases of the Moon: Waxing and Waning
questions.question: Which of these Moon shapes is NEVER seen from Earth?
options: Lit on both edges with a dark curved bite in the middle
A thin crescent with its horns pointing away from the Sun
A half circle lit on the side nearer to the Sun
A gibbous shape lit on more than half of its disc
questions.explanation: The line separating lit and dark parts is a single smooth curve, so the Moon is never lit on both edges with a dark middle. Crescent, half and gibbous shapes, with the lit side towards the Sun, are all real phases.

questions.topic: Locating the Moon in the Sky
questions.question: Malini saw the Moon overhead in the sky at sunset. What phase was it, and was it waxing or waning?
options: A half Moon, waning
A half Moon, waxing
A full Moon, waning
A crescent Moon, waxing
questions.explanation: Overhead at sunset means the Moon is about a quarter of the way around the sky from the Sun — a half Moon. Since a waning half Moon is overhead at sunrise, the one overhead at sunset must be the waxing half Moon.

questions.topic: Locating the Moon in the Sky
questions.question: Ravi says he saw a crescent Moon rising in the east as the Sun set. Kaushalya says she saw a gibbous Moon in the east during the afternoon. Who is telling the truth?
options: Only Ravi
Both of them
Only Kaushalya
Neither of them
questions.explanation: A Moon rising in the east at sunset is opposite the Sun and must look full, not crescent — so Ravi's claim is impossible. A waxing gibbous Moon rises in the afternoon and can be seen in the east, so Kaushalya's report is possible.

questions.topic: Locating the Moon in the Sky
questions.question: Vaishali saw the Moon in the sky from sunset right through to sunrise. Which phase must it have been?
options: New Moon
Waxing crescent
Waning half Moon
Full Moon
questions.explanation: Only a full Moon rises at about sunset and sets at about sunrise, staying up all night. A new Moon is invisible, and crescents and half Moons are up for only part of the night.

questions.topic: Why Phases Happen: The Ball-and-Lamp Model
questions.question: On days when a crescent Moon is visible, the lit part of the crescent always faces
options: towards the Sun
away from the Sun
towards the north
towards the horizon
questions.explanation: The crescent's bright edge faces the Sun because that is the side receiving sunlight; moving a finger from the Sun to the Moon along the shortest path crosses the lit part first.

questions.topic: Why Phases Happen: The Ball-and-Lamp Model
questions.question: In the 'Discover' activity, what does the line joining the two tips of a crescent Moon correspond to?
options: The edge of the Earth's shadow
The diameter of the Moon
The Moon's orbit around Earth
The radius of the Moon
questions.explanation: The two horns of the crescent lie at opposite ends of the lit half's boundary, so the line joining them is a diameter of the Moon's disc.
